task.description:
Queue task 692 (issue). Read docs/issues/ISS-0692.yaml in full for the complete finding -- do not rely on this summary. SECURITY-REVIEWER flagged, during REQ-362's Step 2c gate, that the visual-regression-testing design (lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md) commits UAT screenshot baselines to git (test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/), with superseded baselines retained forever in git history, and the design states zero PII/redaction/synthetic-data policy. REQ-362 itself only exercises an unauthenticated static page, so nothing in REQ-362's own diff currently violates an invariant -- the gap is that a FUTURE requirement pointing this mechanism at a real authenticated gui_screen UAT scenario (explicitly deferred per the design's own OQ-4/2.4/3.6/4.4) would have no guardrail preventing real tenant PII (candidate names, emails, etc.) from becoming a permanently git-committed artifact.

Step 0.5 (registry lookup): check docs/issues/*.yaml for a prior resolved entry about PII handling in committed test fixtures/artifacts. Note any match (or none) in your result.summary.

Step 1 (diagnose): this is a design-gap issue, not a code defect -- there is no failing test to run. Your diagnosis must state: (a) exactly which design sections need to change and what they must say (synthetic/seeded-data requirement, a redaction step, or an explicit accepted-risk statement -- your call which is appropriate, with reasoning), (b) whether web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts's acceptBaseline/rebaseline functions need an actual code change now, or whether stating the policy in the design is sufficient because no authenticated scenario currently adopts this tooling (AC2 in ISS-0692.yaml is explicitly conditional: 'If a redaction or synthetic-data mechanism is chosen, it is implemented...' -- read that condition carefully against current usage before concluding implementation is required now), (c) affected files and what a fix needs to change. Do NOT implement the fix yourself -- produce the diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: Registry lookup performed and result stated (match or no match)
Diagnosis states which design sections must change and the specific policy content required (not just 'add a policy')
Diagnosis explicitly rules on whether code implementation is required now vs. design-only, with reasoning tied to current usage of the mechanism
next_action names CODE-DESIGNER as the next step

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): searched all 350 docs/issues/*.yaml for PII/redaction/synthetic-data-in-committed-fixtures matches. Grepped 'PII' (only hit is ISS-0692 itself), 'redact' and 'synthetic' (33 files). None is a match for this symptom class: ISS-0388/0391/0393/0526 concern disclosed-synthetic vs. real *functional* scenario fixtures (Simulation.Runner input data), an honesty/provenance concern, not PII-in-a-permanently-committed-image; ISS-0600/0647/0651/0653 concern API-response field-level redaction (FieldGrants), unrelated to UI screenshots. No prior resolved entry exists for this exact gap -- not a recurrence.

STEP 1 (diagnosis). Note on artifact location: lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md and web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts do NOT exist on the current branch (feature/WF03-ISS0692-20260916) or on main -- they exist only on origin/feature/WF02-REQ362-20260916 (commits 389fdbf8 'feat' and bc053cfc 'design', both still unmerged). Read both from that ref via `git show`. CODE-DESIGNER must apply the fix on whichever branch that work currently lives on (or after it merges) -- flag this to ORCH if it isn't obvious at dispatch time.

(a) WHICH SECTIONS MUST CHANGE, AND WHAT THEY MUST SAY. The design's current §1.3 ('Distinctness from transient screenshots') states baselines 'are committed to git ... this is durable fixture data' with zero data-sensitivity caveat; §2 (accept action) and §4 (re-baseline action) likewise have no precondition on the *content* of what gets persisted. Required change: add an explicit data-sensitivity policy, e.g. new §1.5 'Data-sensitivity policy for baseline content' (or fold into §1.3), stating as a binding invariant, not a suggestion: 'Any gui_screen expected outcome accepted or re-baselined through this mechanism (§2, §4) must be captured against synthetic/disclosed-fictional actor and tenant data only -- never real tenant PII (candidate names, emails, etc.). This is not a new practice: it is the same discipline already governing every scenario file under test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/ today (verified by reading test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/swiftroute/tenant-onboarding-happy.yaml -- its actor \"Alice Bauer\" / \"alice.bauer@swiftroute.example\" / \"swiftroute.bpm.example\" are disclosed-fictional, per that corpus's existing header-comment discipline, same as ISS-0388/0391's synthetic-fixture disclosure). This design's own job is to make that invariant explicit and binding specifically for this mechanism, because unlike a transient screenshot, a baseline accepted here is permanently retained (§1.3's own git-history point) -- so a future scenario author pointing this at a screen seeded with real data has no guardrail today.' Also add one sentence to §2.2 and §4.1 cross-referencing this new section as a precondition of calling accept/rebaseline, and add a row/line to §7's AC map noting this policy addresses AC-1's/AC-2's implicit data-handling scope. Replace ISS-0692's own suggestion of 'or an explicit accepted-risk statement' -- accepted-risk is NOT the right call here (reasoning below), so the design should resolve this as a stated decision, not leave it as an open question in §8.

Policy choice and reasoning (synthetic-data requirement, not redaction, not accepted-risk): (1) Redaction (masking/blurring regions of the PNG before persist) is a poor fit for THIS specific mechanism: phase 2 (§3.4) is explicitly designed as an unconditional, mechanical pixel-diff with no loosened tolerance -- a redaction mask must be bit-for-bit stable across every future run or it becomes a second source of spurious diffs, directly fighting the design's own 'auto-fail is unconditional' intent (§3.4). A synthetic-data requirement has no such conflict -- the screen simply never contains real data to begin with, so pixel stability is unaffected. (2) Accepted-risk is not defensible given real tenant PII would be a permanent, git-history-retained artifact (§1.3's own point) -- this is exactly the kind of tenant-data exposure the project's security invariants exist to prevent (SECURITY-REVIEWER raised the finding, not a nice-to-have). (3) Synthetic/seeded data costs nothing new to adopt -- the existing UAT scenario corpus (16 files use gui_screen today, confirmed via grep, including several authenticated screens: swiftroute/tenant-onboarding-happy.yaml, platform/tenant-branding-applied.yaml, platform/tenant-switch-cache-isolation.yaml, etc.) is ALREADY entirely synthetic/disclosed-fictional -- so this design change asks nothing beyond restating an existing, already-followed practice as an explicit invariant of this one mechanism.

(b) IS A CODE CHANGE TO acceptBaseline/rebaseline REQUIRED NOW? No. Read AC2's condition precisely: 'If a redaction or synthetic-data mechanism is chosen, it is implemented...'. A synthetic-data-only *policy* is not something acceptBaseline/rebaseline's code can mechanically enforce -- 'is this screenshot's on-screen data synthetic' is a content judgment made by the scenario author / UAT-RUNNER at authoring/dispatch time, not a property the function can statically verify from a PNG buffer or a BaselineKey. This is unlike a redaction mechanism, which WOULD be actual code (a pixel-masking transform applied inside acceptBaseline before fs.copyFileSync) -- but redaction is not the chosen policy (see reasoning above), so there is no redaction code to implement. Additionally, confirmed against current usage: no authenticated gui_screen scenario has yet been run through this mechanism for real -- design §2.4/§3.6/§4.4 all explicitly defer the 'exercised for real' baseline-accept/pixel-diff/re-baseline runs to TEST-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV at a later WF-02 step; zero PNGs exist under test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/ today (directory does not exist in the tree on either the current branch or origin/feature/WF02-REQ362-20260916 at the design/feat commits). So AC2's implementation clause is not triggered: nothing has been 'chosen' that requires code, and no baseline has yet been committed that the policy would need to retroactively apply to. Design-only fix is sufficient to close this gap now.

Optional (CODE-DESIGNER's discretion, not required to satisfy AC2): add a one-line docstring note to acceptBaseline/rebaseline in web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts pointing callers at the new design section ('callers must only invoke this against scenarios whose captured data is synthetic/disclosed-fictional -- see design §1.5') so the invariant is visible at the call site, not only in the design doc. This is a comment-only change, not an implementation of a redaction/synthetic-data mechanism, so it does not trigger AC2's implementation clause either way.

(c) AFFECTED FILES AND WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md -- primary fix target; add new §1.5 (or extend §1.3) stating the synthetic-data-only invariant per (a) above, cross-reference from §2.2/§4.1, update §7's AC map, and remove/resolve this as a stated decision rather than leaving §8 to gain a new open question. web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts -- no functional change required; optional docstring cross-reference only, CODE-DESIGNER's call. No other files require changes to close ISS-0692 (docs/agents/uat-scenario-schema.md and .claude/agents/uat-runner.md were checked and need no change -- the scenario corpus already follows the synthetic-data discipline this design change merely makes explicit for this one mechanism).

issues.note: Design-gap issue confirmed via direct reading of both artifacts (fetched from origin/feature/WF02-REQ362-20260916 since neither file exists on the current branch or main). No code defect, no failing test -- diagnosis is a design-section-content specification for CODE-DESIGNER.
